answer: In an island gem exchange, every opal shipment entering the inlet receives one signed cargo ID from an independent dock scanner. Agents may bid to verify its weight, but the exchange pays only one valid report per cargo ID and checks a random sample against the dock scale before releasing escrow. Each bid locks a bond that is slashed for copied or false readings. Creating more agent accounts cannot create more cargo IDs or rewards, while honest agents can compete on distinct shipments.
